correctness.rationale: The DN follower blocks have exactly the claimed Sturm tridiagonal spectrum. For n/sqrt(t) going to infinity their far block has heat trace length times the bulk diagonal plus o(1); the near block converges spectrally to a mixed Neumann-Dirichlet Gaussian heat trace. Every minimizing scaled distance is forced into a finite positive compact interval and to the unique minimizer of G. The uniform quadrature error is O(sqrt(t)/length)+O(exp(-3t)); analytic derivative comparisons cover x<=0.7 and x>=1, while an exact-rational 40-panel certificate proves strict G convexity on [0.7,1] and signs at the two rational brackets. The finite short/long time statements follow from the first heat coefficient and the exact smallest grounded eigenvalue. All crucial normalizations and quantifiers are stated, and the new packaged verifier was executed successfully.

value.rationale: The objective measures total finite-time squared consensus error across orthonormal follower initial conditions, a standard finite-horizon network-control metric. The theorem gives a universal coefficient in the natural diffusive scaling regime, for all growing path/time sequences and every optimizer, with an exact theta-characterization and rigorous numerical interval. This distinguishes transient design from both short-time degree preference and fixed-size long-time spectral-gap preference. It is a structural location law for an infinite family, not an arbitrary small-graph computation or routine reformulation of a known stationary optimum.
